# Sortino ratio (`sortino_ratio`)

*Category: Risk-adjusted performance · Nature: estimated · Unit: ratio · Formula id: `sortino_ratio@v1` · Methodology 0.1.0*

## 1. What does it measure?

Average return in excess of the target per unit of downside deviation, annualized.

## 2. Formula

```text
P * mean(r_t - MAR) / ( sqrt((1/n) sum min(r_t - MAR, 0)^2) * sqrt(P) ), MAR = 0
```

## 3. Required inputs

Periodic simple returns with a regular frequency.

## 4. Is higher or lower better?

Higher is better.

## 5. Plain-language interpretation

Like the Sharpe ratio, but only losing periods count as risk.

## 6. Professional interpretation

Sortino & Price (1994) with MAR = 0 and full-sample downside deviation. Downside deviation from few losses is noisy; the ratio is undefined without losses.

## 7. Assumptions

- Target (MAR) of 0% per period.
- Square-root-of-time scaling.

## 8. When can it be misleading?

- Very few losing periods: the denominator is unstable.
- Returns are smoothed or stale.

## 9. Minimum sensible data

At least 2 observations and at least one period below the target; low confidence below 3 years. (policy `ratio_standard`: Risk-adjusted ratios: at least 2 observations; low confidence below 3 years, moderate below 5 years.)

## 11. Sources

- Sortino, F. A., & Price, L. N. (1994). Performance Measurement in a Downside Risk Framework. Journal of Investing, 3(3), 59-64.
- Bacon, C. R. (2021). Practical Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement (2nd ed.). Wiley.

## 12. OpenFactsheet convention

MAR = 0 per period; full-sample denominator; annualized by sqrt(P) (decision 0006).
